summary: Moves through a long list split into pages, like the token table or the review history. The first and last pages stay visible; the rest collapse into ellipses.
whenToUse: Long, stable lists where users need to know where they are and jump back: token tables, audit logs.
Below the list it controls, aligned with the list's start or end edge.
compact in narrow spaces (side panels, mobile) and in card footers.
whenNotToUse: Feeds the user skims once: load more or infinite scroll fit better.
Fewer than about 25 items: show them all.
Steps of a task: use a stepper.

dos.title: Keep the page in the URL
dos.text: Reloading or sharing the link should land on the same page. Control page and onPageChange from your router.

donts.title: Hiding previous and next at the ends
donts.text: Disabled previous on page 1 keeps the layout still and tells the user they are at the start.

accessibility: A nav landmark named "Pagination" (override with aria-label when a page has several).
The current page button has aria-current="page" and an ink fill, not color alone.
Page buttons are named "Page N"; previous and next are named "Previous page" and "Next page" and are disabled at the ends.
Ellipses are icons hidden from assistive tech.
In compact, the "Page 3 of 12" text is a polite live region, so page changes are announced.
contentGuidelines: Use "Previous" and "Next", not arrows alone or "Back" and "Forward".
Show the total count of items near the list ("412 tokens"), not inside the pagination.
